selected_evidence.requirement: opsadmin created with the specified public key installed for SSH access
selected_evidence.summary: opsadmin account created, authorized_keys populated with the exact requested ed25519 key (700/600 perms), and confirmed still present with the correct key content after restart

selected_evidence.requirement: SSH restricted to key-based authentication only
selected_evidence.summary: 99-key-only.conf drop-in applied; sshd -T for user opsadmin shows pubkeyauthentication yes / passwordauthentication no / kbdinteractiveauthentication no / authenticationmethods publickey both before and after the restart, and opsadmin's password is locked

selected_evidence.requirement: sshd able to run at all (fixed missing host keys and /run/sshd, otherwise SSH access would be impossible)
selected_evidence.summary: sshd -t failed with 'no hostkeys available' then 'Missing privilege separation directory /run/sshd'; fixed by generating host keys and creating /run/sshd, then added a tmpfiles.d rule since none existed to recreate the directory on boot
Captured pre-restart boot_id (92ec88af...), ssh.socket active state, listening port 22, and opsadmin/key-only policy state

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled and acknowledged; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset while down, then succeeded with a new boot_id (0ca69e26...), proving an actual restart occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of SSH service, opsadmin config, and key-only policy
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot: ssh.socket active, /run/sshd recreated via tmpfiles rule, opsadmin account and authorized_keys intact, password still locked, sshd -T confirms key-only policy still enforced, and a live TCP handshake to port 22 returned the SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p banner

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== create opsadmin =="
sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin
echo "== set up .ssh =="
sudo -n mkdir -p /home/opsadmin/.ssh
sudo -n tee /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys >/dev/null <<'EOF'
ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAINMKA2+oNHxgmpABaV61Sar8lVW2YxSL8Aw9d7b5yLh1 os-comparison@example.invalid
EOF
sudo -n chmod 700 /home/opsadmin/.ssh
sudo -n chmod 600 /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
sudo -n chown -R opsadmin:opsadmin /home/opsadmin/.ssh
echo "== lock password (no password login) =="
sudo -n passwd -l opsadmin

echo "== enforce key-based auth cluster-wide sshd config =="
sudo -n tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
PubkeyAuthentication yes
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
AuthenticationMethods publickey
EOF

echo "== validate sshd config =="
sudo -n sshd -t

echo "== reload ssh (socket-activated, ensure config applied) =="
sudo -n systemctl restart ssh.socket
sudo -n systemctl kill -s HUP ssh.service 2>/dev/null || true

echo "== verify opsadmin =="
getent passwd opsadmin
sudo -n cat /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys
echo "== verify effective sshd auth config =="
sudo -n sshd -T -C user=opsadmin | grep -Ei '^(passwordauthentication|pubkeyauthentication|kbdinteractiveauthentication|authenticationmethods)'
